A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same political-bias measurement study. All 18 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original results from 88,110 responses across 11 LLMs, stance-classifier validation, and prompt and reformulation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the classifier evaluation and appendix robustness analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes from describing human-assigned proposition labels to GPT-4 ground truth checked against 40 manually labeled items. However, v1 already includes automatic-labeling prompts in Appendix A. The PDFs do not establish whether the underlying procedure changed or its description was corrected. The remaining measurement and classification pipeline is retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 89 PCT and EVS/WVS propositions and political-bias task with 30 prompt variants. The newly listed propositions and source counts document existing coverage; they do not establish additional datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated model set, PCT-versus-WVS comparison, zero-shot-versus-fine-tuned stance classifier, and GPT-4-versus-Llama reformulation comparison are retained. Newly cited studies are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 revises the reported annotation and validation protocol: v1 describes two authors labeling the propositions, whereas v2 specifies GPT-4 labels verified using a 40-item human sample. This is a reported protocol revision, not evidence that the main experiments were rerun. Model configurations, response counts, classifier training/test sizes, and confidence filtering remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The proposition-label verification is recast as a robustness check of GPT-4 against human annotations. The prefix, Likert, survey-source, and alternative-reformulation analyses already appear in v1 and remain in v2. In particular, v1 Appendix H and v2 Appendix I contain the same Llama reformulation results.

E5.justification: The reported Cohen's kappa values of 0.77 and 0.76 change attribution from agreement between human annotators to agreement between manual annotations and GPT-4, changing the stated statistical comparison. Three generations per prompt and 10,000-sample bootstrap estimation of 95% confidence intervals are retained.

E6.justification: The redrawn appendix plot reassigns nine PCT model series while preserving the corresponding WVS values. For example, the displayed PCT Likert bias for mistral-7b-instruct-v0.1 changes from about -0.32 to +0.38, and GPT-4's opinion-prefix bias from about -0.03 to -0.46 (v1 Figure 5; v2 Figure 6). These materially change model-specific findings despite unchanged main results and no stated replacement protocol. Section 2 also adds literature-search findings.

T1.justification: The political-bias definitions and Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Expanded arguments about survey validity do not introduce new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims: a theory-grounded, prompt-sensitive measure, generally stronger leftward bias in instruction-tuned models, instability across prompts, and PCT exaggeration for some models.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive arguments about PCT items' dependence on English-speaking contexts and their stability across countries and time, strengthens the rationale for WVS, and connects prefixes to practical usage. The ethical statement is corrected to say the research does not prescribe an ideological stance. The principal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the anonymized resource placeholder with a concrete code/data repository address and supplies all 89 propositions with their labels in Tables 10–12, plus source-label counts in Table 1. These additions make the exact measurement inventory substantially more auditable. Existing hardware, generation settings, and classifier hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds related-work comparisons with Stammbach et al. (2024), Röttger et al. (2025), and Bang et al. (2024), alongside citations supporting survey validity and automated annotation. The basic contribution positioning remains unchanged; numerous other reference edits are publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: v2 expands the survey-validity and prompting explanations, inserts an inventory appendix, updates affiliations and contact information, and makes grammatical and bibliographic edits. The main section sequence and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the nine prefix-based scatter panels with eleven model-based grouped-bar panels, changing axes, legends, and comparison organization. It also adds the proposition inventory and count tables, expands the related-work table, and captions previously unnumbered prompt and hyperparameter tables. Several retained displays are relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The complete proposition inventory, explicit resource address, and fuller methodological explanations improve auditability. However, the redesigned appendix chart reassigns PCT series across model names, producing substantial changes that conflict with retained findings, such as GPT-4's near-neutral opinion responses. The PDFs do not resolve the competing result assignments or explain their relationship to the unchanged main results. These documentation gains and evidential inconsistencies prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
